text:
maria: quick q — we're updating the node SDK and want to be explicit: if a client calls /v1/embeddings with a single string (not an array), should the server coerce to an array or return 400? also what's the expected output for an empty string item?

aj: short answer: hosted API will coerce a lone string -> [string] for backward compat. we won't break old clients that pass a bare string. empty string is allowed and returns a deterministic embedding (not an error). the vector shape is consistent with the model profile (e.g., 1536 floats for the default open-embed model).

maria: thanks — do we document that somewhere or is this an implicit behavior? want to make sure SDKs don't have to special-case unknown hosts.

aj: we'll document and add a minor SDK patch to mirror server behavior. doc note will say: "input: string or array[string] accepted; string coerced to single-item array. null items are rejected with 400. empty string returns an embedding."

lena: clarifying truncation: if the input exceeds token limit, do we reject, truncate, or return a partial embedding? clients need predictable semantics for regressions.

aj: we do per-item token truncation (not reject) for embeddings: we truncate to model max context and compute embedding on truncated text. we'll log a regression alert if truncation rate for a customer spikes. truncation policy: prefer right-truncation for text -> we trim the tail.

kevin: what about batch limits? if someone sends 5k items in one request, do we 413 or stream partial responses? need to know for SDK chunker.

aj: server returns 413 with error code `batch_too_large` and includes `max_batch_items` in the error body. current hosted default = 1024 items per request. Dedicated customers can raise this via config but SDK should chunk to 1024 by default. we'll add an SDK helper `chunkInputs(inputs, max=1024)`.

maria: can we include a small curl example in the docs showing coercion?

aj: yep, we'll add this to the changelog. example:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-v1","input":"single string item"}'
```
server will treat that the same as: `{"input":["single string item"]}`

lena: edge-case: mixed arrays with `null` and `""` — what should clients expect?

aj: `null` => 400 with message `null_items_not_allowed`. `""` => valid and returns embedding for empty string. We'll add a compact table in docs.

kevin: how about output shape for multi-model catalog? do we include `vector_dim` in the response meta so callers don't have to assume?

aj: good call — we'll add `model_dim` in the response metadata object, e.g. `embedding: [...], model: "open-embed-v1", model_dim: 1536`. makes validation easier.

maria: perfect. can you drop a tiny changelog PR and flag me for review?

aj: will do. PR + docs + SDK patch today. cc @kevin for chunker tests. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: SDK patch v0.12.3 scheduled for rollout to canary docs site at 2026-02-12T15:00Z — will post release note when live. :robot_face:

kevin: thanks — i'll add chunking tests and a test for `null` vs `""` items in the e2e suite.

maria: awesome, thanks team. this clears the ambiguity for product and support.
